presentation.balanced_omissions: Detailed package tables, exact command listings, and edge-case explanations remain in the complete reading view and Deep dive source panels.

slides.title: MileStone
slides.lede: One Android app for rewards balances and Amex card benefits.
points: Reads each program's own website in a WebView.
Stores sign-ins and rewards data on the phone.
Uses one app module with domain, data, sync, and UI packages.
Top-right Search separates stored Rewards and Benefits results.

slides.title: Program Refresh
slides.lede: A refresh reuses the program's own profile and saved session.
points: Scheduled and attended refreshes may use a saved sign-in.
The 15-minute keep-alive does not type passwords.
A visible refusal pauses automatic sign-in; an unfinished form remains a distinct stop.

slides.title: Benefits Pages
slides.lede: Rewards leads to the card's activity page or its view-all list.
points: Scroll and settle checks wait for the page's own content.
An available activity link wins over a partial Rewards post at the readiness cap.
A late lower section can wait within the supplied 20-second page maximum.

slides.title: Card Switching
slides.lede: The selected card and its tracker content must both change correctly.
points: Press the existing card-switcher option.
Carry a document-local note across an in-place address change.
Reject old trackers instead of assigning them to the next card.

slides.title: Read Deadline
slides.lede: The complete benefits read shares one 120-second deadline.
points: A page gets at most 20 seconds within the remaining budget.
Reserve the full first-page maximum before allowing a second page.
Cut second pages before leaving later cards unread; once cut, later second pages stay cut.

slides.title: Benefits Display
slides.lede: Local display settings complement section-scoped storage that preserves unread data.
points: Institution tiles open their own card lists with a clear Back hierarchy.
Four outlined categories have saved sorting, a Completed last filter, and Show/Hide controls.
Matching offline artwork and conservative duplicate display retain issuer rows and enrollment details.
Yellow alerts can be acknowledged; only a successful relevant refresh can reintroduce source alerts.

slides.title: Privacy
slides.lede: Only named fields are read, and diagnostics remain count-only.
points: Exact host and path checks, a nonce, and message-field checks guard the bridge.
Account keys, full card numbers, cookies, and sign-in data stay out of diagnostics.
Private captures stay local; notifications use private lock-screen text.
Search query, result tab, and scroll positions stay in the navigation entry, in memory.

slides.title: Verification
slides.lede: Unit, WebView, and live checks prove different parts of the flow.
points: JVM tests cover protocol, budget, state, and section replacement.
Emulator fixtures drive the real script and bridge.
Phone checks record fresh per-card counts and read times without account text.

source_values.text: MileStone is a native Android app (com.bendourthe.milestone) that shows the points, miles, and rewards cash of the user's loyalty programs on one dashboard, and, for American Express, each card's benefits on a Benefits tab. It reads each balance from the program's own website inside an embedded browser (Android WebView) after the user signs in once, and keeps those sign-ins alive in the background. Account balances are read automatically; optional welcome-bonus spending is entered locally. No server is involved: every balance, sign-in, and saved password stays on the phone.
The remote origin is https://github.com/bendourthe/MileStone.git. main is the release branch and develop is the integration branch. The version is the latest heading in the root CHANGELOG.md.
Kotlin, Jetpack Compose (Material 3), Gradle with a version catalog (gradle/libs.versions.toml).
compileSdk 37, targetSdk 36, minSdk 29.

Build types: debug, release, and capture. capture is a debug copy with the suffix .capture and the label "MileStone Capture"; it adds a "Capture page" action that saves a page for selector work. Captures are copied to the PC through app/src/capture/sanitize_capture.py, which strips identifiers on the way, and inspected only through inspect_capture.py, which prints structure with text masked. CI never builds it (ADR-0001).
The debug build adds a "Site check" launcher entry (app/src/debug) for testing whether a program's site works in the embedded browser.

The canonical validation entrypoint is scripts/validate.py. The fast profile checks the private-input boundary, Python and extractor syntax, and handbook freshness. The full profile adds validation-helper tests, unit tests, lint, debug and local capture builds, instrumented-test compilation, coverage, Room schema checks, handbook browser checks, and secret scanning. Full validation needs the Playwright dependency in scripts/requirements-validation.txt and its Chromium browser, plus installed Gitleaks or the documented preloaded Docker image; the profile does not install those tools.
Local full gate, run from the repository root in PowerShell:
python scripts/validate.py --profile full --quiet

Use python scripts/validate.py --profile fast --quiet for the smaller checks. --list --json lists a profile's commands without running them or writing reports. Profiles write results under reports/ by default; python scripts/validate.py --profile report --quiet aggregates existing receipts without rerunning checks. The release profile packages a clean committed source archive, verifies reproducible archive bytes and safe paths, and records version, commit, and SHA-256 metadata. It does not build an APK, use signing secrets, rerun tests, publish, or tag a release; debug sideloads remain separate.
The local emulator runtime gate is separate from full:
python scripts/validate.py --profile platform --quiet

This profile accepts only emulator-5554, verifies ro.kernel.qemu is 1, and sets the test child's ANDROID_SERIAL to that emulator before connectedDebugAndroidTest. Do not run connected tests against the owner's phone: installing the test app clears its sign-ins. Instrumented-test compilation in full is not runtime proof.

CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) is configured to validate pull requests to develop or main on Ubuntu 24.04 with Java 17. After preparing the pinned dependencies, it runs .validation-venv/bin/python scripts/validate.py --profile full --platform ci-linux --quiet, installs the Android 36 Google APIs x86_64 image, verifies KVM acceleration, boots an isolated headless emulator-5554, and runs .validation-venv/bin/python scripts/validate.py --profile platform --platform ci-linux --quiet. Emulator cleanup, report aggregation, and report upload are configured to run even after failure. CI result requires the validation job to succeed for those target branches. The explicit ci-linux full profile still excludes the local-only capture build under ADR-0001. This describes the configured workflow; hosted execution has not yet been observed for the local v0.4.0 candidate.
All code is in the single app module under com.bendourthe.milestone.
Package
Responsibility
domain

Models (Program, ExtractionSpec, BenefitsSpec, SyncResult, FailureReason, BalanceUnit), card and benefit models with stable keys (Benefits.kt: a card is its program plus last digits; a benefit is its card plus title or the issuer's list key plus period), BenefitPeriods (period labels to end dates), repository interfaces, catalog search, and the dashboard use case. No Android types.
data.catalog

StaticCatalogRepository: the 14 programs, their hosts, sign-in and balance URLs, and fixture-verified XPath or CSS balance selectors, and for American Express the benefits pages and selectors (AMEX_BENEFITS, ADR-0008). Hosts come only from the feasibility record.
data.db

Room database version 4 (loyalty_accounts, balance_snapshots, cards, benefits, benefit_reminders; cards, benefits, and reminder records cascade from their account or card), RoomCardRepository, schema exports in app/schemas/.
data.session
TinkSessionStore: encrypted per-program session metadata (connected and verified times), never cookies.
data.credentials
CredentialVault: saved sign-ins sealed with AES-256-GCM under an Android Keystore key (StrongBox when available), one file per program in noBackupFilesDir/signins (ADR-0004).
data.settings
DataStore preferences for dashboard sorting and card-specific benefit sorting, collapsed categories, alert acknowledgements, optional welcome-bonus setup, and section-read outcomes.
sync
SyncManager, the single writer of balances and statuses, with per-program throttle, backoff, and refresh reasons (ON_START, MANUAL, KEEP_ALIVE); ForegroundSyncObserver refreshes when the app opens.
sync.webview

The login bridge: WebViewConfig (hardened settings and a full-height layout, without which Chromium lays pages out with a zero viewport height and every vh length is 0), HostPolicy (exact-host allow list), SessionProfiles (one WebView profile and cookie store per program), BridgeSession (the page-state machine), LoginBridge (WebView glue), HeadlessWebViewBalanceSource (refresh without UI), HeadlessWebViewBenefitsSource (the benefits read, card by card), and AutoSignInSupport.
sync.extract

BridgeProtocol (messages to and from the page script, with benefits messages accepted only from the catalog's benefits pages), BenefitsReader (field checks, caps, and section rules), BenefitAmountParser, PageStateClassifier, and BalanceParser.
sync.mfa
OneTimeCodeInbox and SmsCodeReceiver: texted sign-in codes held in memory for five minutes, matched by sender keywords, handed out once.
sync.background

KeepAliveScheduler, KeepAliveReceiver, and KeepAliveService (a refresh every 15 minutes as a short dataSync foreground task), ScheduledRefreshScheduler (an alarm at the next scheduled midnight, allowed while the phone idles), VirtualDisplayWebViewHost (an off-screen WebView), BenefitReminders (the daily credit reminder check, its private notifications, and its 9:00 alarm), and the notification channels.
ui

MainActivity, the navigation host (Rewards, Benefits, Settings), the dashboard, the Benefits tab and card pages (ui.benefits), the program catalog, settings, and the sign-in sheet (AuthWebViewModal, AutoSignInDialog). ui.theme holds the single dark teal color scheme and AuroraBackground, a slow animated gradient that stays still when system animations are off.
AppContainer wires these together by hand; there is no dependency-injection framework.

The user adds a program from the catalog and signs in inside AuthWebViewModal. The page script app/src/main/assets/extract.js runs only on the program's exact hosts, reads the balance element named by the catalog selector, and posts it back; SyncManager stores it.

SyncManager refreshes programs in a hidden WebView that reuses the program's own cookie store. The user's schedule in Settings (every day, every Sunday by default, or the last day of the month, each at midnight) sets an alarm that refreshes every balance older than that time and may sign in. Opening the app refreshes a program only when it was neither updated nor tried since that scheduled time; a failed program waits for the next scheduled time or the user's Refresh. Every 15 minutes in the background, the keep-alive reads connected programs to keep their sessions alive. Reads share two fetch slots and sign-ins run one at a time; a sign-in the user just started skips that queue.

When a session has ended and the user saved an automatic sign-in, the hidden browser opens the program's sign-in page directly (and skips the session read when the last one already found the session ended), and the page script fills the saved username and password, ticks "remember this device", prefers a texted code, and enters a code that arrives by text. A site that asks for the username alone first gets the username, then at most one more fill on its password page. The script submits with the form's Sign in or Continue button and never presses a show-password toggle. Passwords are typed when the user opens MileStone or at the scheduled refresh, never by the 15-minute keep-alive (ADR-0005). A sign-in counts as refused only when the site shows an error with its form; a form back without an error is unfinished and may be tried again. A refused password is never retried: automatic sign-in pauses for that program until the user taps Sign in or Refresh on its tile, which tries the saved sign-in once more and opens the site for the user if it stops again, or until a sign-in succeeds. A background refresh that needs the user posts a "needs you" notification.

Signing out or removing a program cancels its running refresh or sign-in, erases its WebView profile's cookies and storage at once, and deletes its saved sign-in; a profile still held by a live WebView is deleted at the next app start.

After a saved American Express balance (not for the keep-alive), a separate benefits read opens the Amex Rewards page in the same profile. The page script reports the card switcher's cards (names and last digits only), then presses the switcher option for each next card and follows the page's own activity link for cards that have one. Cards without an activity page post their Rewards trackers before opening their own view-all link for the full list. Each page waits for its own content markers, scrolling to load lower sections and checking that counts and height have settled; after a switch, the new card's trackers must replace the previous card's. At the 15 s Rewards readiness cap, an available activity link is followed even while the page is still growing; a missing lower section can wait up to the app's page timeout, at most 20 s. One deadline bounds the whole benefits read to 120 s, cutting second pages before leaving cards unread when time is short. The read never signs in and never reads an account key (ADR-0008). SyncManager replaces only the sections actually read: a failed view-all page keeps the previous list, and an unread card keeps its previous benefits. A card is removed only when a complete card list no longer shows it. Count-only diagnostics identify page kind, readiness, wait time, card index, and total read time. The Benefits tab groups cards by program with matching offline artwork, benefit counts, yellow alert counts, next open credit, and freshness. The card display and acknowledgement rules are described below.

Once a day at 9:00 and when the app opens, the reminder check posts one private notification per statement credit and period when part of the credit is unused and its period ends within 7 days (monthly), 14 (quarterly), or 30 (half-year and yearly), never from benefits read more than 8 days ago and never twice for the same credit and period. Settings has a Benefit reminders switch, on by default.

Add program opens on programs not added yet, with a filter for Added and All programs; added programs carry a green outline. Programs whose sites do not work in the embedded browser cannot be added, and tapping one says so. Pulling the dashboard down asks "Refresh all programs?" before refreshing everything, since a full refresh can take minutes; the top refresh button refreshes at once. An added program's menu offers Refresh, Sign out, and Remove; "Open in app or browser" was removed (ADR-0002, ADR-0003, ADR-0007).

Benefits starts with one tile per tracked institution that supports card benefits, with card and active-alert counts. Pressing an institution opens only its cards; card Back returns to that card list and list Back returns to the institutions. Connected institutions remain visible before their cards are read. Tapping a supported program on Rewards opens its card list directly; reminders open the named card with the same parent hierarchy. Known Platinum, Business Platinum, Hilton Surpass, and Delta Gold products use distinct bundled public artwork; an unknown product uses a generic offline card icon. Each card page groups Welcome bonus, Credits, Spend trackers, and Other. The top-right sort menu offers Name A-Z (the default), Name Z-A, Deadline soonest, and Largest amount remaining within each category, with unknown dates or amounts last. The separate top-right filter menu holds Completed last, applied before the selected sort. Both choices are saved per card. Outlined, counted category headings have explicit Show/Hide controls and collapse independently, with Other initially collapsed. Completed items retain their category with a check and strike-through; an unknown completed kind remains in Other rather than being inferred from its amount. Completed credits show a full progress bar with the earned/target amount beside it. The display uses a positive stored target, then positive stored earned amount, then a single leading dollar amount in the completed credit title; unknown or multiple dollar amounts are not inferred. This display-only fallback does not change stored issuer rows. Unfinished credits retain actual progress and the inline ratio; other trackers keep their existing amount labels. Enrolled appears beside the title before the completed check, while Enrollment required remains in the body.

The local welcome-bonus form groups amount digits with commas while preserving exact cents and cursor positions. Saved whole-dollar values reopen without .00; fractional cents remain precise. Standalone numbers in the Reward field and local reward description also group with commas, while raw free text, codes and dates remain unchanged. The optional deadline displays YYYY-MM-DD separators during entry and accepts a calendar selection. Choosing a calendar date changes the draft only; Save commits the setup. Calendar dates are converted in UTC so the selected calendar day stays unchanged across time zones. Invalid amounts or dates show field-specific errors.

A listed entry merges into a tracker only when the same-card title/period match is unambiguous and enrollment statuses do not conflict. Description and enrollment details remain visible on the copied tracker. Raw issuer rows stay stored for refresh, reminders, and count verification. Different periods or ambiguous matches remain separate.

Yellow alerts appear above the card artwork and categories. They identify enrollment requirements, unused credits near their established reminder deadline, stale reads, and a listed-benefits section that failed to refresh. Acknowledge hides one alert and updates its count without changing enrollment, issuer rows, or notification records. Acknowledgements survive navigation and restart. Only a successful relevant section read can reintroduce a still-applicable source alert; tracker period changes do not change a retained listed enrollment's identity. Failed or cancelled reads cannot reset it. Local welcome-bonus deadline alerts instead follow the saved manual setup.

Each successful section replacement increments the card's Room read generation in the same transaction. The following DataStore outcome binds to that generation and read time and advances only the sections actually covered. A mismatch or unavailable outcome is labeled unknown; an older list is explicitly identified when only trackers refreshed. A whole-card timestamp alone never proves list freshness. The additive version 3 to 4 migration preserves accounts, benefits, enrollment, and reminder records.

Welcome-bonus setup stores optional local spent amount, target, deadline, and reward label separately from issuer data and account balances. Plain decimal validation rejects malformed, negative, overflow, or scientific-notation amounts before expansion; targets must be positive, dates valid, and reward labels at most 120 characters. Fields identify and focus validation errors. A failed settings write keeps the previous state and shows visible feedback rather than claiming it saved.

The local v0.4.0 candidate places Search with the top-right dashboard and Benefits actions, with no new bottom tab. Search separates Rewards and Benefits results and searches added programs, stored cards, and the benefits produced by the existing display model. Rewards result tiles show only the program image, name, and stored points. Benefits matches have independently collapsible program, card and canonical section groups with chevrons. Program headings use larger themed text with a small bundled program image; compact card headers show a small bundled card image, name, and ending and always open the exact card, with a separate right-side chevron for collapse. Single-line title-only benefit tiles retain canonical card-page order and open the full benefit tile. A program result scrolls to its exact Rewards tile with a temporary four-second outline. A program-only query such as Amex includes all of that added program's stored cards and canonical benefits. Mixed contextual queries combine an item's own text with program or card context and still require at least one own-text token; canonical source titles remain aliases. Query, selected result tab, group collapse choices, and per-tab scroll state stay in memory for the Search navigation entry. Exact source and revision checks precede result navigation; a benefit result temporarily reveals its category without changing saved collapse settings. Back preserves the originating viewport and the Search result position while their entries survive. Read and stale-selection failures use generic retry or reselect notices. The installed metadata remains v0.3.1, version code 4; v0.4.0 is not released. See Global search for corpus boundaries, matching, and reveal validation.

Logs name programs and hosts only, never full URLs, page text, balances, cookies, passwords, or codes. DiagnosticLog also appends these lines to no_backup/diagnostics.log (capped at 512 KB), so a stop can be diagnosed after the phone's log buffer rotates; on a debug build, read it with adb shell run-as com.bendourthe.milestone cat no_backup/diagnostics.log.

A card is identified on the phone by its last digits only. Full card numbers, account keys, and membership numbers are never stored, logged, or sent; the page script strips grouped digit runs, identifier-like tokens, and account-key-shaped runs before posting, and benefit reminders show only "A card benefit expires soon" on the lock screen.
Real captured pages live only in the gitignored app/src/test/resources/fixtures-private/; committed fixtures in app/src/test/resources/fixtures/ are hand-written with fake balances.
Cloud backup and device transfer exclude every app data domain (res/xml/backup_rules.xml, res/xml/data_extraction_rules.xml), and the vault sits in noBackupFilesDir, which Android never backs up.

Unit tests (app/src/test, Robolectric where Android types are needed) cover the catalog, Room and its migrations, cards and benefits storage, the vault, the code inbox, the bridge state machine and benefits protocol, SyncManager with its benefits read, period labels and reminders, the Benefits screens, and ExtractorFixtureTest and BenefitsFixtureTest, which run every selector against its synthetic fixture and, locally, its private capture.

Instrumented tests (app/src/androidTest) cover WebView configuration, headless sync and the benefits read against local fixtures (with identifier decoys), a reminder notification, and screenshots of the Benefits screens. Running them uninstalls the app, which clears every sign-in and saved password.
The Amex benefits reader companion describes page readiness, card switching, time limits, and section-scoped storage in more detail. All three sources are included in the offline handbook.

The benefits read starts after a saved American Express balance, in the same program profile. It reads cards and benefit sections from the site's existing controls. It never signs in, composes an account-key URL, or fetches account data from another service.
Page
Role
Successful result
Rewards
Lists the cards and starts a card read
Follows the card's activity link, or posts trackers before following its view-all link
Activity
Holds the full tracker set and list for cards that offer it
Stores every covered section for that card
View-all
Holds the full list for cards without an activity page
Joins the list to the Rewards trackers
Navigation presses the page's own link or card-switcher option. The app accepts benefits messages only on the configured Amex host and page paths, with the expected message nonce and page kind.
The script scrolls to load lower sections. A shape is steady when tracker count, listed-link count, and page height stay unchanged for two seconds. A page with no trackers gets a longer empty settle.

Rewards requires an activity or view-all link, a reached bottom, and settled content. At its 15-second readiness cap, an available activity link is still followed. A missing lower section may wait up to the supplied page timeout, capped at 20 seconds.

Activity requires its own content: the Rewards activity link must be absent, and at least one tracker or listed link must exist. Rewards content under an activity address is never accepted as an activity read.
View-all requires listed content whose count differs from the page it was opened from, then bottom and settle checks. A capped empty list does not erase the previous list.

Before pressing a link, the script leaves a document-local handoff note. An in-place address change adopts that note; a full document load drops it. After pressing an activity link, the script waits for navigation or a bounded unreadable result instead of posting partial Rewards trackers.

The selected card must match the target, and its tracker fingerprint must be nonempty and different from the previous card's. The fingerprint stays inside the script and is never posted. An emptied tracker area is not proof that the new card has loaded.

The switch cap is 12 seconds. A settled empty tracker area with the right markers may become an empty read after that cap. Old trackers still on screen produce a mismatch, preserving the stored card rather than assigning another card's trackers to it.
One deadline covers the whole 120-second benefits read, with margins for script and app cleanup. Each page gets at most 20 seconds and cannot extend the shared deadline.

At a card's first page, the scheduler reserves 20 seconds for its possible second page and 20 seconds for every remaining first page, including the current one. If that time is unavailable, it cuts second pages for this and all later cards. If fewer than 10 seconds remain for another card to start, it leaves that card unread. These cuts preserve stored sections that were not reached.
The 20-second first-page reserve includes a late Rewards lower section. Reserving only 15 seconds could spend time on an earlier activity page and leave the last card unread.

BenefitsCardReads records which sections a card's pages covered. Rewards alone covers tracker sections. A successful view-all adds the listed section. An activity page covers every section. A failed or mismatched view-all keeps the new trackers and the previous stored list.

SyncManager sends those section sets to RoomCardRepository. The repository deletes and replaces only those sections in a transaction under the program lock. A failed card keeps its previous benefits. Cards disappear only when a complete card list no longer contains them.

Completed credit tiles render full progress with the earned/target ratio inline beside the bar. Their display-only target uses a positive stored target first, then a positive stored earned amount, then a single leading dollar amount in the completed credit title. A title with multiple dollar amounts or no usable leading amount supplies no inferred target. The display does not rewrite issuer amounts or stored rows. Unfinished credits retain actual progress and their inline ratio; noncredit trackers retain their existing amount labels. Enrolled appears beside every enrolled item's title, before the completed check when present. Enrollment required remains a body status.

Issuer sections remain the replacement boundary; display categories do not change stored rows. The card's successful-write generation increments inside the same Room transaction as section replacement. After that write, SyncManager records covered section generations in DataStore, bound to the exact Room generation and read time. If the outcome write is unavailable or cancelled, the UI labels list freshness unknown; equal timestamps cannot reuse an earlier generation. Tracker-only success preserves both old listed rows and their older source generation.

The presentation transform retains the original enrollment source when it merges a listed row into a tracker. Alert identity and acknowledgement use that source row and successful section generation, so a changed tracker period cannot revive acknowledged enrollment from an unchanged list. Separate local keys retain sort, collapse, welcome setup, and acknowledgement changes under concurrent writes. The version 3 to 4 migration adds the counter without deleting existing data.

Benefits diagnostics hold fixed page kinds, bounded counts, readiness reasons, wait times, card indexes, and the run total. They do not hold benefit text, amounts, card digits, account keys, page queries, or sign-in values. Card outcomes distinguish read, unread-list, and mismatch results; a read outcome alone does not prove that every benefit was loaded.

Card freshness alone does not prove that its list was refreshed: trackers can be new while a failed list keeps its older contents. The visible per-list freshness note is tracked separately from the extraction fix.

Synthetic WebView fixtures exercise late lower sections, in-place address changes, card switching, view-all navigation, and failed-list preservation. JVM tests cover the protocol, budget, card-read transitions, and real Room section replacement. Private-capture tests run locally, and their contents are never committed or printed.

Instrumented tests run on the emulator only. Running them on the owner's phone uninstalls the app and clears sign-ins. Live phone verification uses adb install -r, keeps the app in the foreground, and records only per-card section counts, enrollment counts, diagnostics, and read times. The database copy used for counts is deleted immediately afterward.

The site can change or load too slowly for the budget. The read preserves sections explicitly left unread, while a capped page can contain only the content loaded before its cap. Card freshness alone is not proof of completeness. Background continuation and automatic retry policy remain separate work. The Benefits display supports card-specific sorting, grouping and collapse, conservative duplicate presentation, local welcome-bonus setup, and yellow acknowledgeable alerts; these do not extend the extraction deadline. The architecture decision is ADR-0008.

Global search is part of the local v0.4.0 candidate. The installed version metadata remains v0.3.1, version code 4; this candidate has not been released. A top-right Search icon sits with the dashboard and Benefits actions and opens a separate navigation entry. Search has Rewards and Benefits result tabs; the existing bottom navigation remains unchanged, with no Search tab. Search uses stored items without signing in, refreshing an account, or making a remote search request.

SearchViewModel builds a snapshot from added accounts, their stored cards and benefits, and per-card display preferences. Cards and benefits are read together through the repository's Room transaction. Programs absent from the user's added accounts are excluded. The snapshot uses BenefitsViewModel.page and BenefitsPresentation.presented, so benefit results follow the destination's displayed rows and conservative duplicate owner. Source titles retained during canonical merging remain search aliases for that displayed benefit; they do not create duplicate results.
SearchViewModel prepares tab partitions, counts, and card groups on its worker dispatcher; the screen reuses those cached projections.

Program names, program identifiers and categories, card names, benefit titles, descriptions, and canonical source-title aliases contribute to matching. Card digits are removed from the matching text. Each compact Benefits card header shows a small bundled card image, name, and ending; freshness remains nonvisual accessibility context outside the matcher. Current monetary values and other internal identifiers are not corpus fields. Rewards result tiles show the program image, name, and stored points only; those stored points do not become a matching field. Compact benefit tiles show a single-line title without details. Stored completion, period and enrollment remain available on the full destination and do not become extra matching fields. Collapsed categories remain searchable because collapse affects visibility rather than membership in the displayed page model.

The query is limited to 256 characters. Matching applies simple Unicode case folding per code point, turns non-letter and non-number separators into spaces, and matches normalized tokens as substrings. The same fold locates context excerpts, including symmetric matches for sigma variants, long s, and the micro sign. When every normalized token matches a program's name or identifier, that program-only query includes all of its stored cards and canonical displayed benefits. For example, Amex includes the added Amex program's stored children without requiring an item token. Mixed contextual queries still require every token to appear in the item's own text or program/card context and at least one token in the item's own title, description, or aliases. Card parent context includes the program identity; benefit parent context also includes the card name. Blank normalized input shows the start prompt rather than all items.

The counted Rewards tab contains matching programs. The counted Benefits tab groups matching cards and compact benefit matches under their program and card headers. Benefit matches retain the category and item order from that card's canonical Benefits page, including its saved sort and Completed last settings. Programs, cards and canonical benefit sections have independent chevron collapse controls, initially expanded. Program headings use a larger title, a distinct theme color, and a small bundled program image, including for benefit-only queries. Compact card headers show a small bundled card image beside the name and ending, without visible freshness detail or a bright outline. Selecting the card header opens its exact card; a separate right-side chevron only expands or collapses its matches. Compact benefit tiles show the matching title on one line with ellipsis for overflow, without details; description and alternate-title matches still lead to the exact full tile. The full benefit remains available at the destination. Without an explicit tab choice, program matches select Rewards; card or benefit matches without program matches select Benefits. Search does not rewrite saved dashboard or card display sorting.

Each snapshot has an opaque, memory-only revision. Selecting a result requires a fresh repository read, unique target membership, equality with the expected source snapshot, and the same observed revision. Stable keys alone cannot authorize opening an item after stored rows or display preferences change. A monotonic query-edit version rejects a delayed selection if the query was edited, even when the text changes back to its original value. The card destination also checks its exact card, ordered benefit rows, and preferences against the snapshot. Benefit reveal validates again after the category layout is ready, before scrolling.

A program result opens the dashboard, scrolls to that exact program and adds a temporary four-second outline. Every card header opens its exact card detail, including a header supplied as context for benefit matches. Its separate chevron changes only the group's expanded state. A compact benefit match opens the full benefit tile on its exact card detail. The existing reveal temporarily expands its category, scrolls to the row, highlights it, and announces its title for accessibility. This temporary expansion does not save a new collapse preference. Explicit Hide dismisses the visit-local expansion so the category can close normally. A missing item, changed source, read failure, or reveal timeout returns a generic notice instead of selecting a nearby row or silently falling back to another card.

Query text, the selected result tab, per-tab scroll positions, group collapse choices, and reveal state belong only to the Search navigation entry's ViewModel in memory. They are not persisted as history, route arguments, or saved instance state. Returning from a result preserves this state while that entry survives; Back from Search returns to the prior screen. The outgoing screen retains its viewport when the bottom bar is hidden, including an end-of-list position. An actual query edit resets both result list positions, group collapse choices, and the explicit tab choice, and Clear empties the query and focuses the field.

Source errors show a retry action. Selection errors use the generic messages "Results changed. Select the item again", "That stored item is no longer available", or "Stored items could not be read. Please retry". Query text is not added to diagnostics, analytics, notifications, or account refresh requests. Search uses stored data; selecting a match does not imply a fresh remote read. Card freshness remains available to accessibility services and on the full destination.

The matcher, snapshot and revision logic, navigation, temporary reveal, and screen behavior need separate checks. Unit tests can prove matching and stale-target rejection, while emulator interaction must confirm the right-side icon, counted result tabs, grouped compact matches, canonical benefit order, exact card-header navigation and independent chevrons, program-only child matching, exact full-tile destination, category reveal, Clear, keyboard, Back, and per-tab scrolling. The local v0.4 candidate's release and independent UI qualification remain separate from this handbook's reproducible build and browser checks.
